title: Käpt’n Börgers Piratennest (PixelPlaza)
lede: A small isometric pirate harbor from the German pixel art community PixelPlaza, with a timber house, a fort wall, a ship, and figures a few pixels tall.
summary: Isometric pirate lair on a rock, with a timber house, a galleon, palms, and turquoise water. Boerger, PixelPlaza, 2008, CC BY-SA 3.0.

source.label: Wikimedia Commons: Pixel-Art Käpt'n Börgers Piratennest.gif

evidence.note: Downloaded the Commons file (216 × 146 px, one frame, about 250 colors) and inspected it enlarged 5× to 1080 × 730 px.

styles.note: Partial fit: hand-placed pixels at a fixed scale with tiny figures, but in the isometric branch that the style record lists as related, with many more colors than the 8-bit core.

context: Commons describes the file as “Artwork from the German pixel art community named PixelPlaza, depicting a pirates’ lair”, author Boerger (@pixelplaza.de), dated 11 April 2008, licensed CC BY-SA 3.0. [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pixel-Art_K%C3%A4pt%27n_B%C3%B6rgers_Piratennest.gif).
Wikipedia names isometric pixel art as a common form, with Habbo Hotel and eBoy as examples. [Wikipedia: Pixel art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixel_art).
observed: A harbor seen from above at an isometric angle, on a white ground: a timber-framed house with a brown roof, a jetty on stilts, a gray stone fort wall, and a tower on a rock.
A brown galleon with two masts lies in turquoise water. A red parrot sits on the wall.
Figures are about 5 to 8 pixels tall.
Walls and roofs follow stepped two-to-one diagonals.
Rock and stone are shaded with many close tones and scattered single pixels, so the texture looks noisy rather than flat.
No smooth gradient appears. White spray pixels mark the waves at the rock.
interpretation: The piece shows the community form of pixel art in the 2000s: a self-contained scene for its own sake, not a game asset.
Its many tones and textured rock move away from the flat 8-bit palette. Use it for the isometric branch, not as a model for interfaces.
borrow: Draw isometric edges with a regular two-pixels-across, one-pixel-down step.
Give tiny figures one bright color each so that they read against a detailed ground.

images.alt: Isometric pixel-art pirate harbor on white: a brown timber house on a jetty, a gray stone fort wall and tower on a rock, palm trees, and a brown two-masted ship in turquoise water.
images.caption: Boerger (PixelPlaza), “Käpt’n Börgers Piratennest”, 2008, [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pixel-Art_K%C3%A4pt%27n_B%C3%B6rgers_Piratennest.gif), CC BY-SA 3.0. Enlarged 4× with nearest-neighbor scaling and saved as PNG.
